name: Cognitive Load Architecture
short_description: How environmental information demands interact with working memory capacity limits, determining task performance, decision quality, and cognitive fatigue.

components.name: Working Memory Load
components.description: Environmental information demands consume working memory capacity; when demands exceed capacity, performance degrades.

components.name: Ecological Rationality
components.description: When environmental information structure matches the heuristic tools available, decision quality improves despite limited processing.

components.name: Hierarchical Control
components.description: Environmental task structure interacts with the cognitive control hierarchy, shaping error patterns and performance.

components.name: Cognitive Offloading
components.description: Legible environments allow offloading of information storage to the environment, freeing internal processing.

design_implications: Minimize extraneous environmental complexity in high-cognitive-demand spaces (hospitals, control rooms).
Provide external information scaffolding (checklists, spatial cues) that reduces reliance on internal memory.
Design task-environment fit: align information layout with the natural decision hierarchy.
Use progressive disclosure in physical spaces — reveal complexity gradually rather than all at once.

confidence_intervals.note: Effect sizes for environmental cognitive load manipulation on task performance.
